content_html:
The adhkar before sleep are the verses and supplications the Prophet ﷺ authentically said when he went to bed: the three Quls with blowing and wiping, Ayat al-Kursi, the end of Al-Baqarah, "Bismika Rabbi wada'tu janbi", the 33-33-34 tasbih, and "Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk" as your last words.

Below: each with source, grading and meaning, a printable table, and what to say if you wake at night.

What are the adhkar before sleep in order?

  1. Make wudu (ablution) and lie down on your right side.
  2. Blow lightly into your palms, recite Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas, and wipe your body. Three times.
  3. Recite Ayat al-Kursi.
  4. Recite the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah.
  5. Say "Bismika Rabbi wada'tu janbi..." or "Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya".
  6. Say SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times and Allahu Akbar 34 times.
  7. End with "Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk..." as your last words.

This order is only an aid to memorising. The Sunnah fixes no binding order, except that the Prophet ﷺ said of al-Bara's du'a: "Make these the last words you speak." Saying only some of them is still good; you need not say all of them every night.

In the Quran, sleep is a kind of lesser death:

﴿اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ الْأُخْرَىٰ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾

"Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term." (Surah Az-Zumar 39:42, translation: Sahih International)

So the bedtime adhkar hand your soul to Allah and close your day with tawhid (affirming His oneness).

What are the Sunnah etiquettes of sleep before the adhkar?

Three Sunnahs come first:

  • Wudu: the Prophet ﷺ told al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: "When you go to your bed, perform wudu as you do for prayer." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 247, Muslim 2710)
  • Your right side: in the same hadith: "Then lie down on your right side."
  • Dusting off the bed: "When one of you goes to his bed, let him dust it off with the inside of his lower garment, for he does not know what came onto it after him." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 6320, Muslim 2714).

Which verses and surahs are recited before sleep?

1. Al-Ikhlas and the two Mu'awwidhat with blowing and wiping (three times)

'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated that every night, when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed, he would put his palms together, blow lightly into them and recite ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ (Al-Ikhlas), ﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ﴾ (Al-Falaq) and ﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ﴾ (An-Nas), then wipe as much of his body as he could, starting with his head, face and the front of his body. He did that three times. (Al-Bukhari 5017)

The blowing is a light breath with a little moisture. Meaning: Al-Ikhlas affirms Allah's oneness, Al-Falaq seeks refuge from every outward evil, and An-Nas from the hidden evil of whispering.

2. Ayat al-Kursi (once)

It begins: "Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep..." (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:255, translation: Sahih International)

Its virtue comes in the story of Abu Hurayrah and the one who kept taking from the charity food, who told him: "When you go to your bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi; a guardian from Allah will stay with you and no devil will come near you until morning." The Prophet ﷺ said he had told the truth though he was a liar, and that he was a devil. Al-Bukhari narrated it (2311) mu'allaq (without a full chain) in definite wording, others connected it, and scholars graded it authentic. It is the greatest verse in the Book of Allah (Muslim 810).

3. The last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah

Verses 285-286 begin: "The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers..." (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:285, translation: Sahih International)

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever recites the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 5009, Muslim 807). Reciting them at bedtime makes sure the night does not pass without them. Scholars explained "suffice him" as protecting him from every harm, or as sufficing him in place of the night prayer; the wording allows both.

4. Surah As-Sajdah and Surah Al-Mulk

Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ "would not sleep until he had recited Alif Lam Mim Tanzil (As-Sajdah) and Tabarakalladhi biyadihil-mulk (Al-Mulk)." (At-Tirmidhi 2892, graded sahih by al-Albani). Any time of the night before sleeping counts.

5. Surah Al-Kafirun

The Prophet ﷺ told Nawfal al-Ashja'i: "Recite Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun, then sleep at its end, for it is a declaration of freedom from shirk." (Abu Dawud 5055, at-Tirmidhi 3403). Al-Albani graded it sahih in Sahih Abi Dawud and hasan li-ghayrihi (sound through support) in Sahih at-Targhib.

What are the authentic duas before sleeping?

1. "Bismika Rabbi wada'tu janbi" (once)

«بِاسْمِكَ رَبِّي وَضَعْتُ جَنْبِي، وَبِكَ أَرْفَعُهُ، إِنْ أَمْسَكْتَ نَفْسِي فَارْحَمْهَا، وَإِنْ أَرْسَلْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا بِمَا تَحْفَظُ بِهِ عِبَادَكَ الصَّالِحِينَ»

Bismika Rabbi wada'tu janbi, wa bika arfa'uh, in amsakta nafsi farhamha, wa in arsaltaha fahfazha bima tahfazu bihi 'ibadakas-salihin.

"In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You take my soul, have mercy on it, and if You release it, protect it with that by which You protect Your righteous servants." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 6320 and Muslim 2714)

2. "Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya"

Hudhayfah said that when the Prophet ﷺ wanted to sleep he would say: «بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا» Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya, "In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live." And when he woke: «الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَمَا أَمَاتَنَا، وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ» Alhamdu lillahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur, "All praise is for Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection." (Al-Bukhari 6312). It is the shortest bedtime dhikr, so learn it first.

3. "Allahumma khalaqta nafsi wa anta tawaffaha"

«اللَّهُمَّ خَلَقْتَ نَفْسِي وَأَنْتَ تَوَفَّاهَا، لَكَ مَمَاتُهَا وَمَحْيَاهَا، إِنْ أَحْيَيْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا، وَإِنْ أَمَتَّهَا فَاغْفِرْ لَهَا، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ»

Allahumma khalaqta nafsi wa anta tawaffaha, laka mamatuha wa mahyaha, in ahyaytaha fahfazha, wa in amattaha faghfir laha. Allahumma inni as'alukal-'afiyah.

"O Allah, You created my soul and You take it back. Its death and its life belong to You. If You keep it alive, protect it, and if You cause it to die, forgive it. O Allah, I ask You for well-being." (Muslim 2712, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both)

Some books add "innaka" ("Allahumma innaka khalaqta"), but Sahih Muslim has "Allahumma khalaqta nafsi".

4. "Allahumma Rabbas-samawati wa Rabbal-ard"

«اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبَّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، رَبَّنَا وَرَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَالِقَ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى، وَمُنْزِلَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ وَالْفُرْقَانِ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَنْتَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهِ، اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الْأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَيْءٌ، وَأَنْتَ الْآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَيْءٌ، وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَيْءٌ، وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَيْءٌ، اقْضِ عَنَّا الدَّيْنَ، وَأَغْنِنَا مِنَ الْفَقْرِ»

"O Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Splitter of the seed and the date stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Injil and the Furqan, I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold. O Allah, You are the First and there is nothing before You, You are the Last and there is nothing after You, You are the Manifest and there is nothing above You, You are the Hidden and there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us and free us from poverty." (Muslim 2713)

5. "Alhamdu lillahil-ladhi at'amana wa saqana"

Anas narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say when he went to bed:

«الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا، وَكَفَانَا وَآوَانَا، فَكَمْ مِمَّنْ لَا كَافِيَ لَهُ وَلَا مُؤْوِيَ»

Alhamdu lillahil-ladhi at'amana wa saqana, wa kafana wa awana, fakam mimman la kafiya lahu wa la mu'wi.

"All praise is for Allah who fed us, gave us drink, sufficed us and gave us shelter. How many there are who have no one to suffice them and no one to shelter them." (Muslim 2715)

6. "Allahumma 'Alimal-ghaybi wash-shahadah"

The Prophet ﷺ taught it to Abu Bakr and said: "Say it in the morning, in the evening and when you lie down in your bed." (Abu Dawud 5067; at-Tirmidhi 3392, who said hasan sahih). We explain it in the virtues of the morning and evening adhkar.

7. "Allahumma qini 'adhabaka yawma tab'athu 'ibadak"

Hafsah narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ wanted to sleep, he put his right hand under his cheek and said: «اللَّهُمَّ قِنِي عَذَابَكَ يَوْمَ تَبْعَثُ عِبَادَكَ» Allahumma qini 'adhabaka yawma tab'athu 'ibadak, "O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants." (Abu Dawud 5045). Al-Albani graded it sahih without the addition "three times" in that narration, so say it once; repeating it as a du'a is no problem.

8. SubhanAllah 33, Alhamdulillah 33 and Allahu Akbar 34

Fatimah asked the Prophet ﷺ for a servant to help with the housework. He came to her and 'Ali at bedtime and said: "Shall I not guide you to something better than what you asked for? When you lie down in your beds, say SubhanAllah thirty-three times, Alhamdulillah thirty-three times and Allahu Akbar thirty-four times. That is better for you than a servant." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 5361, Muslim 2727)

That makes one hundred. Some narrations put the takbir first or give 34 to the tasbih; there is flexibility. Do not confuse this count with the adhkar after salah.

9. The du'a of al-Bara': your last words before sleep

The hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib has two authentic narrations. Al-Bukhari (6313):

«اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ نَفْسِي إِلَيْكَ، وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ، وَوَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ، وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ، رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً إِلَيْكَ، لَا مَلْجَأَ وَلَا مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلَّا إِلَيْكَ، آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ، وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ»

Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk, wa fawwadtu amri ilayk, wa wajjahtu wajhi ilayk, wa alja'tu zahri ilayk, raghbatan wa rahbatan ilayk, la malja'a wa la manja minka illa ilayk, amantu bikitabikal-ladhi anzalt, wa binabiyyikal-ladhi arsalt.

"O Allah, I submit my soul to You, I entrust my affair to You, I turn my face to You, and I lean my back on You, out of hope in You and fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You revealed and in Your Prophet whom You sent."

In the narration agreed upon (al-Bukhari 247, Muslim 2710) it begins «اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ» ("O Allah, I submit my face to You") and ends: "If you die that night, you die upon the fitrah (the natural faith of Islam). Make these the last words you speak." When al-Bara' repeated it saying "wa rasulika" (and Your Messenger), the Prophet ﷺ corrected him: "No: and Your Prophet whom You sent." So keep to "wa nabiyyika".

What do I say if I wake up during the night?

If you wake up and turn over in bed

The Prophet ﷺ said:

«مَنْ تَعَارَّ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي، أَوْ دَعَا، اسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ، فَإِنْ تَوَضَّأَ وَصَلَّى قُبِلَتْ صَلَاتُهُ»

"Whoever wakes up at night and says: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir. Alhamdu lillah, wa subhanallah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and the praise, and He has power over all things. All praise is for Allah, glory be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no might nor power except with Allah), then says: Allahummaghfir li (O Allah, forgive me), or makes any du'a, it will be answered. And if he makes wudu and prays, his prayer will be accepted." (Al-Bukhari 1154, from 'Ubadah ibn as-Samit)

Ta'arra means waking with a sound or a turn. So when you wake at night, say this before reaching for your phone, then make du'a. And Mu'adh narrated: "No Muslim sleeps in remembrance and purity, then wakes at night and asks Allah for good of this world and the Hereafter, except that He gives it to him." (Abu Dawud 5042, sahih per al-Albani)

It is also reported that when the Prophet ﷺ turned over at night he said: «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ، رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ» La ilaha illallahul-Wahidul-Qahhar, Rabbus-samawati wal-ardi wa ma baynahumal-'Azizul-Ghaffar, "There is no god but Allah, the One, the Prevailing, Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving." Narrated by an-Nasa'i (al-Kubra), Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim; al-Albani graded it sahih (Sahih al-Jami' 4693), while Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah held it to be a saying of 'Urwah ibn az-Zubayr.

If you wake up frightened

The Prophet ﷺ said: "When one of you is frightened in his sleep, let him say: A'udhu bikalimatillahit-tammati min ghadabihi wa 'iqabihi wa sharri 'ibadih, wa min hamazatish-shayatini wa an yahdurun (I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His anger, His punishment and the evil of His servants, and from the whispers of the devils and their coming to me), and it will not harm him." (At-Tirmidhi 3528; similar in Abu Dawud 3893; graded hasan by al-Albani)

«إِذَا فَزِعَ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي النَّوْمِ فَلْيَقُلْ: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ غَضَبِهِ وَعِقَابِهِ وَشَرِّ عِبَادِهِ، وَمِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ، فَإِنَّهَا لَنْ تَضُرَّهُ»

If you see a dream you dislike

"If one of you sees a dream he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times, seek refuge with Allah from Shaytan three times, and turn from the side he was lying on." (Muslim 2262). In the hadith of Abu Qatadah, he should tell no one, and it will not harm him (al-Bukhari 7044, Muslim 2261). The "spitting" is a light blow with hardly any saliva.

If you wake for the night prayer or Fajr

Say: «الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَمَا أَمَاتَنَا، وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ» "All praise is for Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection." (Al-Bukhari 6312). When the Prophet ﷺ woke at night he recited the last ten verses of Al 'Imran, from ﴿إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:190, translation: Sahih International) to the end (al-Bukhari 183, Muslim 763). If you wake near dawn, see when its time begins in Fajr prayer time.

Are all the popular bedtime adhkar authentic?

Some widely shared bedtime adhkar carry counts and virtues that are not established:

  • Surah Al-Waqi'ah every night against poverty: the hadith "Whoever recites Surah Al-Waqi'ah every night will never be struck by poverty" was graded weak by Imam Ahmad, Abu Hatim, al-Albani and others. Reciting it is good, but not for this virtue.
  • Inventing counts: such as Ayat al-Kursi seven times with a special virtue. Keep to the narrated count.
  • Changing the wording: such as "wa rasulika" for "wa nabiyyika".

Unsure of a dhikr's grading? Check the Dorar hadith encyclopedia (Arabic) before sharing.

How can I keep up the adhkar before sleep?

  1. Start small: the Mu'awwidhat, Ayat al-Kursi and the du'a of al-Bara', under five minutes.
  2. Add one dhikr a week; you will know the full list in about two months.
  3. Say them before picking up your phone in bed, so sleep does not beat you to it.
  4. Leave the tasbih for last, counted in the dark with no paper.
  5. Track yourself nightly in the daily worship tracker.

Rafiq Al-Taa, our free Islamic app at Farhoon (Arabic interface), has the sleep and waking adhkar from Hisn al-Muslim (Fortress of the Muslim) and a tasbih counter for the 33 and 34, with no ads and no account. It is coming soon to Google Play.

How do I teach my children the bedtime adhkar?

Start with "Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya" because it is short, then the Mu'awwidhat with blowing and wiping over their head, which they enjoy. See the plan by age in daily adhkar for kids.

Summary

The bedtime adhkar are few in words and great in effect, ending with "Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk". If you wake at night, say the dhikr of "whoever wakes up at night", then make du'a. This summarises scholars' views; for your own situation, ask trusted scholars in your country.

faq.q: Do the adhkar before sleep have to be said in a set order?
faq.a: There is no binding order for the bedtime adhkar in the Sunnah, so you may begin with any of them. The only explicit instruction is about the du'a of al-Bara', Allahumma aslamtu nafsi ilayk, since the Prophet ﷺ said: make these the last words you speak. So it is best to end your adhkar with it.

faq.q: How many times do I recite the three Quls before sleep?
faq.a: You cup your palms, blow lightly into them and recite Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas, then wipe as much of your body as you can with them, starting with your head and face. You do this three times, as in the hadith of 'A'ishah in Sahih al-Bukhari (5017). The blowing is a light breath that may carry a little moisture.

faq.q: Is the tasbih before sleep 33 or 34?
faq.a: What is established in al-Bukhari and Muslim from the hadith of 'Ali is SubhanAllah thirty-three times, Alhamdulillah thirty-three times and Allahu Akbar thirty-four times, making one hundred. Some narrations put the takbir first or give the thirty-four to the tasbih, and there is flexibility, but the well-known form is thirty-four takbirs.

faq.q: What should I say if I wake up in the middle of the night?
faq.a: Say: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir, alhamdu lillah, wa subhanallah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, then say: Allahummaghfir li, or ask for whatever you wish. The Prophet ﷺ promised that it would be answered, as in Sahih al-Bukhari (1154).

faq.q: Can I read the bedtime adhkar from my phone?
faq.a: Yes, you may read them from a phone or a sheet of paper, and the reward comes from saying them. It is better to memorise them gradually so you can say them in the dark without a screen, and to say them before scrolling on your phone rather than after, so sleep does not overtake you first. They are gathered in the sleep chapter of Hisn al-Muslim.

faq.q: Can a menstruating woman recite Ayat al-Kursi and the Mu'awwidhat before sleep?
faq.a: A menstruating woman may say dhikr and make du'a without any disagreement. As for the verses, most jurists do not allow her to recite them with the intention of reciting Quran, many of them allow it with the intention of dhikr and seeking protection, and the Malikis allow recitation in general. So she should not leave the bedtime adhkar, and should ask scholars in her country for the details.
